pages.summary: The current figure and axes, the root object, and clearing them.
body: Graphics commands work on the current figure and its current axes: `gcf` and `gca` give them, making them when there are none. `gco` gives the object last clicked. `groot` is the root of every graphics object; its properties hold defaults (`set(groot, 'DefaultLineLineWidth', 2)`) and the list of figures. `clf` clears the current figure of its axes and everything in them; `cla` clears the current axes of what is plotted in them, keeping the axes.

examples.title: What is current, and clearing it
examples.output:
ans =

    'matlab.graphics.axis.Axes'

ans =

     1

ans =

     0

ans =

  logical

   1

ans =

  logical

   0

ans =

    'matlab.ui.Root'

pages.summary: Axes made by hand, and how plotting functions prepare them.
body: `axes` makes axes in the current figure, placed by their Position in normalized units of the figure ([left bottom width height], from 0 to 1), or makes given axes current. Plotting functions call `newplot`, which clears the axes unless hold is on (`ishold` tells), so that a new plot replaces the last.

examples.title: An inset
examples.code:
x = linspace(0, 10, 200);
plot(x, sin(x))
inset = axes('Position', [0.6 0.6 0.25 0.25]);
plot(inset, x, exp(-x))
ishold
hold on
ishold

pages.summary: Where the ticks are, and what they say.
body: `xticks` sets (or gives) the positions of the ticks on the x axis, `yticks` and `zticks` on the others; `xticks auto` gives the choice back. `xticklabels` sets the text at the ticks, one label for each, as a cell of texts or a string array.

examples.title: Months on a year's data
examples.code:
plot(1:12, [3 4 6 9 13 16 18 17 14 10 6 4], '-o')
xticks(1:3:12)
xticklabels({'Jan', 'Apr', 'Jul', 'Oct'})
yticks(0:5:20)
xticks

pages.summary: Tick labels turned, written in a format, or written as dates.
body: `xtickangle` turns the x tick labels (in degrees), for long ones. `xtickformat` writes the labels by a pattern: `'%.2f'`, `'%,d'` (thousands parted by commas), `'$%,.2f'`, `'%g°'`, or a name such as `'usd'` or `'percentage'`. `datetick` takes an axis's values as date numbers and labels the ticks as dates, on whole years, months or days as the range suits.

examples.title: Money and long names
examples.code:
bar([1250 3400 2100])
xticklabels({'north region', 'south region', 'west region'})
xtickangle(30)
ytickformat('$%,.0f')
xtickangle

examples.title: Date numbers as dates

pages.summary: The box round the axes, and the proportions of the data and of the plot box.
body: `box on` draws the box's far sides as well as the axes' own lines; in 3-D the back planes are always outlined, and `box on` adds the edges in front when the axes' BoxStyle is 'full'. `daspect` sets the data aspect ratio, how long one unit is on each axis relative to the others ([1 1 1] makes a circle round); `pbaspect` sets the plot box's proportions whatever the data. `'auto'` gives either back to the axes.
syntax: The box twice as wide as high.

examples.title: A circle round, and a wide box
examples.code:
t = linspace(0, 2*pi, 100);
subplot(1, 2, 1), plot(cos(t), sin(t)), daspect([1 1 1]), box off
daspect
subplot(1, 2, 2), plot(t, sin(t)), pbaspect([3 1 1])

pages.summary: A second y axis on the right, and the colours plots take in turn.
body: `yyaxis right` gives the axes a second y axis on the right and makes it the one the next plot uses; `yyaxis left` goes back. Each side has its own limits, ticks and label, and its plots take its colour. `colororder` sets the colours that lines and other plots take in turn (a matrix of rows, or names), or gives them.

examples.title: Temperature and rain
examples.code:
m = 1:12;
yyaxis left
plot(m, [-3 -3 1 6 12 16 18 17 12 7 2 -2], '-o'), ylabel('temperature (°C)')
yyaxis right
bar(m, [40 30 30 35 40 60 75 80 60 55 55 50], 0.4), ylabel('rain (mm)')

examples.title: Three colours of my own

pages.summary: A subtitle under an axes' title, and a title over a grid of subplots.
body: `subtitle` writes a second, smaller line under the axes' title. `sgtitle` writes a title over all the subplots of a figure (or of a tiled layout), above their own titles; `suptitle` is its older name.

examples.title: Four views of one signal

pages.summary: Lines, arrows, boxes and text on a figure, and rectangles and ellipses in the axes.
body: `annotation` draws on the figure itself, in normalized figure units ((0, 0) its lower left corner, (1, 1) its upper right), so that its shapes stay put as the axes change: a line, an arrow, a double arrow, an arrow with text, a rectangle, an ellipse or a text box. `rectangle` draws in the axes' data units, a rectangle with corners rounded by Curvature, an ellipse at [1 1].
syntax: An arrow, its head at the second point.
h = annotation('textbox', [x y w h], 'String', s)
r = rectangle('Position', [x y w h], 'Curvature', [cx cy])

examples.title: A peak pointed out, a region boxed
examples.code:
x = linspace(0, 10, 300);
plot(x, exp(-(x - 4).^2) + 0.3*exp(-(x - 8).^2/0.2))
annotation('textarrow', [0.25 0.39], [0.85 0.88], 'String', 'main peak')
annotation('textbox', [0.62 0.55 0.25 0.1], 'String', 'small one here', 'EdgeColor', 'none')
rectangle('Position', [7.2 0 1.6 0.45], 'Curvature', 0.3, 'EdgeColor', 'r')
rectangle('Position', [3 0.85 2 0.3], 'Curvature', [1 1])

pages.summary: Properties of graphics objects: set and read.
body: `set` gives objects new property values (a name and a value at a time, or a struct of them; several objects at once). `get` reads one property, or all of them as a struct. The same can be written with a dot, h.LineWidth = 2, but `set` takes several objects and properties at once.

examples.title: Two lines at once

pages.summary: Graphics objects found by their properties, the children of an object, and an object's figure or axes.
body: `findobj` searches the objects under a parent (the root unless given) for those whose properties match: a name and value, a pattern (`-regexp`), objects having a property (`-property`), joined by `-and` (the default), `-or`, `-xor` and turned round by `-not`; `-depth` limits how far down it goes. It leaves out objects whose HandleVisibility is off, which `findall` finds too. `allchild` gives every child, hidden ones included; `ancestor` the figure or axes an object is in.

pages.summary: Copies of graphics objects, arrays to hold them, and whether handles are valid.
body: `copyobj` copies objects with everything under them into a new parent: a line into other axes, axes into another figure. `gobjects` makes an array of empty placeholders to fill with graphics objects in a loop. `ishandle`, `ishghandle` and `isgraphics` say which handles are valid graphics objects (not deleted); `isgraphics` also checks the type.

pages.summary: Drawing now, while a program runs, and plots that fetch their data again.
body: Figures are drawn when the program pauses or ends; `drawnow` draws them at once, so that a loop shows its progress, and runs the callbacks of what was done meanwhile. It waits until the page has drawn them, so a loop goes no faster than its pictures. `snapnow` does the same. `refresh` and `shg` are accepted and have no effect. `refreshdata` sets a plot's data again from the expressions in its XDataSource and YDataSource, evaluated in the workspace.
syntax: No more often than the screen shows.

examples.title: A line that follows a variable

pages.summary: Movie frames: a figure as a picture, frames to pictures and back, and playing them.
body: `getframe` takes the figure or axes as drawn on the screen as a frame, a struct whose cdata is the picture (rows by columns by 3 of uint8); it needs the figure on the screen, so it runs in the page. `frame2im` gives a frame's picture, `im2frame` makes a frame of a picture (an RGB array, or indices with a colormap), and `movie` plays a struct array of frames in the axes.

examples.title: Frames of pictures, and a program that films a wave

pages.summary: A figure saved as a picture or a vector file, copied, and its paper orientation.
body: `saveas` writes a figure to a file whose kind its extension sets: .png, .jpg, .bmp and .tif pictures, or .svg, .pdf and .eps, which keep lines and text as such (or a .fig figure file). `exportgraphics` does the same for a figure or axes with a resolution, and `print` with device options (`-dpng`, `-dpdf`, `-r300`). `copygraphics` copies the figure to the clipboard as a picture. These draw the figure, so they run in the page. `orient` sets the paper orientation for printing.

examples.title: The paper, and a program that saves three ways
examples.output:
ans =

    'portrait'

ans =

    'landscape'


function saveAll(fig)
saveas(fig, 'plot.png')
exportgraphics(fig, 'plot.pdf', 'Resolution', 300)
print(fig, 'plot.svg', '-dsvg')
end

pages.summary: Figures saved in a figure file (.fig), and opened again with everything in them.
body: `savefig` writes figures to a .fig file (a MAT-file holding the figure as a tree of properties), and `openfig` makes them again: axes, lines, surfaces, patches, images, text, controls and menus, with their properties. `hgsave` and `hgload` do the same for figures or other graphics objects, `hgload` setting properties given on what it opens.

examples.title: A figure saved, closed and opened again

pages.summary: Points and keys from the person at the screen: clicks in a figure, and text placed by a click.
body: `ginput` waits for n clicks in the current figure and gives their positions in the axes' data units (and which button), ending early at Enter. `waitforbuttonpress` waits for a click or a key. `gtext` waits for a click and puts text there. They need someone at the page.

examples.title: A program that draws through clicked points
examples.output:
function pick()
plot(0, 0), axis([0 10 0 10])
title('click five points')
[x, y] = ginput(5);
hold on, plot(x, y, 'o-'), hold off
gtext('the last one')
end

pages.summary: Editing and exploring a figure on the screen.
body: `plotedit on` turns a figure's edit mode on: a click picks a part of the figure for the property editor, which `inspect` opens beside the figure, showing an object's properties, each with a field that suits it, and the figure's objects as a tree. The figure window has its own tools for zooming (or scrolling), panning (dragging) and turning a 3-D view, and data tips; `zoom`, `pan`, `rotate3d`, `datacursormode`, `brush`, `linkaxes`, `linkprop` and `whitebg` are accepted and have no effect.

examples.title: Settings that change nothing here
examples.code:
plot(1:10)
zoom on
pan off
rotate3d on
datacursormode on
linkaxes(gca)

pages.summary: The camera moved about the axes, and a light placed by angles.
body: The axes are drawn as a camera sees them: from campos toward camtarget (the middle of the axes unless set), camup pointing up on the screen. `camorbit` turns the camera about the target by angles in degrees (as dragging does), `camroll` turns the picture about the line of sight. `lightangle` places a light by azimuth and elevation, as `view` counts them.
syntax: Turned about the line of sight.

examples.title: A surface seen round the side
examples.code:
surf(peaks(25)), shading interp
camtarget
camorbit(40, 0)
camroll(10)
round(camup, 4)
lightangle(-45, 30);

pages.summary: Groups of graphics objects, moved together by a transform, and objects turned about an axis.
body: `hggroup` makes a group: objects made with it as their Parent are shown, hidden and deleted together. `hgtransform` makes a group drawn through a 4-by-4 transform, Matrix, which `makehgtform` makes from translations, scalings and rotations (radians); setting Matrix moves everything in the group, while their own data stay. `rotate` turns objects' data about an axis by an angle in degrees.
syntax: A group drawn through a transform.

examples.title: A shape turned and moved, twice

pages.summary: The ticks, labels and radius limits of polar axes.
body: Polar axes have a radius axis and an angle axis. `rticks` and `thetaticks` set (or give) where their ticks are (angles in degrees, every 30 unless set); `rticklabels` and `thetaticklabels` what the ticks say; `rlim` the radius limits.

examples.title: A compass rose of wind
examples.code:
th = linspace(0, 2*pi, 9);
polarplot(th, [4 6 3 2 5 7 4 3 4], '-o')
thetaticks(0:45:315)
thetaticklabels({'E', 'NE', 'N', 'NW', 'W', 'SW', 'S', 'SE'})
rlim([0 8])
rticks([2 4 6 8])
rticklabels({'2 m/s', '4', '6', '8'})
thetaticks
